old_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of a single diamond ring placed on an open book. The ring is positioned upright, and the camera remains stationary. The book beneath it has visible text, though it is not entirely legible due to the angle and focus on the ring. The background is dark, which makes the ring stand out prominently. The lighting is soft yet focused, highlighting the sparkle and brilliance of the diamond. The ring slowly rotates on the book, providing different angles and perspectives. This movement allows viewers to appreciate the intricate details and craftsmanship of the jewelry. The shadow of the ring is cast on the book, adding depth to the scene. The overall atmosphere is one of sophistication and elegance, emphasizing the beauty and value of the ring.
original_wisa_caption: The video showcases a close-up view of two elegant diamond rings placed on an open book. The rings are positioned side by side, with one slightly overlapping the other. The book beneath them has visible text, though it is not entirely legible due to the angle and focus on the rings. The background is dark, which makes the rings stand out prominently. The lighting is soft yet focused, highlighting the sparkle and brilliance of the diamonds. As the video progresses, the camera slowly pans around the rings, providing different angles and perspectives. This movement allows viewers to appreciate the intricate details and craftsmanship of the jewelry. The shadow of the rings is cast on the wall behind, adding depth to the scene. The overall atmosphere is one of sophistication and elegance, emphasizing the beauty and value of the rings.
caption: The video showcases two diamond rings standing upright on a white sheet printed with rows of text, against a dark background. Their silhouettes are nearly merged, so the pair reads as a single band with one bright stone head. As the viewing angle shifts, the overlapping forms separate into two distinct rings. The right-hand ring reveals a pavé band, while the left-hand ring shows a plainer band. The cast shadow changes from a single loop into two overlapping loops and shifts its shape. Printed rows of text appear to shift and tilt across the frame. Star-shaped glints flash from the stones and metal as the angle changes. The rings remain upright and in contact with the paper throughout the excerpt. Their relative positions open from alignment into side-by-side separation, with sparkle and shadow still shifting across the scene.

Audit this candidate caption against the actual chronological images, and correct factual errors.
This is a TEMPORALLY CROPPED EXCERPT from a longer video, not a complete event or a loop.
The first view may already be mid-action; the last view need not contain completion. Different
endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.
Do not shorten a rich caption into a terse technical checklist. Avoid annotation phrases such as
'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

Return JSON {"decision":"keep|edit", "issues":[{"quote":"exact span in candidate caption",
"problem":"concrete visual mismatch or unsupported assertion"}], "caption":"complete final caption",
"length_note":"empty unless required"}. Keep means unchanged caption and no issues. An edit
must actually correct the cited issue. This is a fallible automatic review, not proof of correctness.

review_issues.quote: Printed rows of text slide across the paper and tilt in the frame.
review_issues.problem: The text is printed on the static sheet and does not slide across it; the rings stay rooted on the same paper. The apparent movement and tilt of the text are produced by the changing viewpoint/camera angle, so describing it as sliding 'across the paper' misattributes a viewpoint effect to motion on the surface.
